Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of algebraic spaces.
If <MATH_0002> is locally of finite presentation, flat, and surjective and
<MATH_0003> is locally Noetherian, then <MATH_0004> is locally Noetherian.

Choose a scheme <MATH_0001> and a surjective <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism <MATH_0002>.
Choose a scheme <MATH_0003> and a surjective <ACCENT_0002>tale morphism
<MATH_0004>. As <MATH_0005> is surjective, flat, and locally of
finite presentation the morphism of schemes <MATH_0006> is surjective, flat, and
locally of finite presentation. In this way we reduce the
problem to the case of schemes (as being locally Noetherian for <MATH_0007> and <MATH_0008>
is defined in terms of being locally Noetherian of <MATH_0009> and <MATH_0010>, see
Properties of Spaces,
Section <REF_0001>).
In the case of schemes the result follows from
Descent, Lemma <REF_0002>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of algebraic spaces.
If <MATH_0002> is locally of finite presentation, flat, and surjective and
<MATH_0003> is regular, then <MATH_0004> is regular.

By
Lemma <REF_0001>
we know that <MATH_0001> is locally Noetherian.
Choose a scheme <MATH_0002> and a surjective <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism <MATH_0003>.
It suffices to prove that the local rings of <MATH_0004> are all regular local
rings, see
Properties, Lemma <REF_0002>.
Choose a scheme <MATH_0005> and a surjective <ACCENT_0002>tale morphism
<MATH_0006>. As <MATH_0007> is surjective and flat the morphism of schemes
<MATH_0008> is surjective and flat. By assumption <MATH_0009> is a regular scheme
in particular all of its local rings are regular (by the lemma above).
Hence the lemma follows from
Algebra, Lemma <REF_0003>.
